prompt.context_jp: 東京・景凡社の面接室に、七度目の挑戦者___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 七度目の挑戦者___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The chapter opens by introducing a new figure in the interview room. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is the narrator introducing a brand-new figure into the scene — classic new-information が. The reader doesn't yet know who this seventh challenger is; が spotlights them as fresh information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 「七度目の挑戦者」 as a known topic the reader has been tracking. But this is the very first sentence of the chapter — no topic has been established yet.

contrast_examples.jp: 面接室に挑戦者が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: A challenger was standing in the interview room. (new to us)

contrast_examples.jp: その挑戦者は七度目の受験だった。
contrast_examples.en: That challenger (already known) was on her seventh try.

prompt.context_jp: 河野悦子にとって、道___『Lassy』の編集者になるか、諦めて別の人生に切り替えるか、どちらかしかない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 道___『Lassy』の編集者になるか…どちらかしかない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 道 (path/option).

feedback.correct_en: 道 is the topic being defined — the sentence tells us *as for her path*, only two options exist. は frames the topic so the predicate can explain what it is.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 道 as new/identifying information, as if answering 'what exists?' That clashes with the explanatory 'A か B か, どちらかしかない' structure.

contrast_examples.en: As for the options, there are only two.
(Lo and behold,) there are two paths. (presentational)

prompt.context_jp: 華やかな照明のもと、モデルや業界人が交ざり合うロビーには、意外な顔___紛れ込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ロビーには、意外な顔___紛れ込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 意外な顔.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence presents a surprising new entity — 'an unexpected face' — into an already-set scene (ロビーには). が carries this presentational, 'look who showed up' feeling.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 意外な顔 as an established topic, but this face is being revealed to the reader for the first time right here.

contrast_examples.jp: 人ごみに意外な顔が紛れていた。
contrast_examples.en: An unexpected face was mixed in the crowd. (newly revealed)

contrast_examples.jp: 意外な顔は貝塚だった。
contrast_examples.en: The unexpected face was Kaizuka. (identifying a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 雛壇に並んだ亀井さやか___、モデルたちを一人ずつ、値踏みするような眼差しで検分していく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 亀井さやか___、モデルたちを…検分していく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the already-introduced editor-in-chief.

feedback.correct_en: Kamei Sayaka is already established in the scene and the sentence describes *what she is doing* — a textbook topic marker は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make her a fresh subject being singled out, but she's the known authority whose behavior the narration is tracking.

contrast_examples.jp: さやかはモデルを見た。
さやかがモデルを見た。
contrast_examples.en: It was Sayaka who looked at the models. (identifies who)

prompt.context_jp: 暗がりの中で、彼女は自分の胸___思いのほか騒ぐのを感じていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女は自分の胸___思いのほか騒ぐのを感じていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 胸 inside the embedded clause.

feedback.correct_en: The whole clause 「自分の胸が…騒ぐの」 is the object of 感じていた. Inside such embedded/subordinate clauses, the subject takes が, not the topic は. 彼女は is already the outer topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would clash because the sentence already has a topic (彼女は). Having two は's for two different referents in one clause is unnatural; the inner subject needs が.

contrast_examples.en: As for my heart, it was racing. (standalone topic sentence)

prompt.context_jp: 血の気___音を立てて引いていくのが分かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 血の気___音を立てて引いていく…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 血の気 (the color draining).

feedback.correct_en: This is a vivid in-the-moment sensation — 'the blood drained from her face.' Spontaneous physical reactions in narration take が: they're reported as events happening, not topics being discussed.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a general statement about 血の気 as a topic, losing the sudden, event-like feel this dramatic moment needs.

contrast_examples.en: The blood drained from her face. (event)

prompt.context_jp: 米岡光男___机に突っ伏し、痩せた肩を小刻みに震わせているのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 米岡光男___机に突っ伏し…震わせているのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle as the narrator discovers Yoneoka's state.

feedback.correct_en: Etsuko has just walked back and spots an unusual scene. The narrator presents what she sees — Yoneoka slumped and shaking — as fresh observation. Presentational が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat Yoneoka as the ongoing topic of discussion, but he's being introduced into this moment as a surprising discovery.

contrast_examples.jp: 見ると、米岡が泣いていた。
contrast_examples.en: When she looked, Yoneoka was crying. (discovered)
Yoneoka (as a topic) is a crybaby.

prompt.context_jp: デスクに山と積まれたゲラの背表紙___、蛍光灯の下でひっそりと光っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ゲラの背表紙___、蛍光灯の下でひっそりと光っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in this scene-setting description.

feedback.correct_en: A new morning scene is being painted; the spines of the proofs are introduced as part of the visible scenery. Descriptive/presentational が is standard here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the spines are an already-established topic being commented on. They're simply part of the newly-opened scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 机にゲラが積まれていた。
contrast_examples.en: Proofs were piled on the desk. (scene description)

contrast_examples.jp: そのゲラは分厚かった。

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩の視線___その一部始終を捉えている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 藤岩の視線___その一部始終を捉えている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Fujiiwa is silently watching the exchange.

feedback.correct_en: The narration shifts to a short, focused reveal: *it is Fujiiwa's gaze that catches every detail.* This exhaustive/spotlighting function is a hallmark of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make this a general comment about 藤岩の視線 as topic; the dramatic effect of pointing out *whose* gaze it is would be lost.

contrast_examples.jp: 藤岩の視線が全てを見ていた。
contrast_examples.en: It was Fujiiwa's gaze that saw it all.
Fujiiwa's gaze (as a topic) is cold.

prompt.context_jp: 私が校閲し終えたあとに 校閲部の誰か___こっそり付箋 付けたんだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 校閲部の誰か___こっそり付箋 付けたんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Etsuko reveals the real culprit. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 誰か (someone — an unknown, indefinite person) virtually always pairs with が. It introduces a new, unidentified agent of the action.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰かは is grammatically unusual — you can't take 'some unidentified person' as a known topic. が is required for unspecified existents.

prompt.context_jp: あれ___受賞できなかったなんて 絶対おかしいと⇒ 五十六賞を主催していた出版社に 抗議の手紙を書きました
prompt.prompt_jp: あれ___受賞できなかったなんて絶対おかしい。
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiiwa insists that *that very book* should have won. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Fujiiwa is singling out *that one book* as the subject that shockingly failed to win — exhaustive/identifying が. The emphasis is on 'that one in particular.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would soften the emphasis and turn it into a general comment. Fujiiwa's indignation hinges on singling out that specific debut as the thing that was wronged.

contrast_examples.jp: あれが受賞できないのはおかしい。
あれは受賞しなかった。

prompt.context_jp: じゃあ その方に 再校をお願いしたいって 先生___おっしゃったんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 先生___おっしゃったんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiiwa clarifies who said it. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: She's identifying *who* said it to answer 'who requested this?' — exhaustive-listing が ('It was 先生 who said so'). The point is pinpointing the speaker.
feedback.incorrect_en: 先生は would just report what sensei said as a general topic; here the focus is defensively specifying *that it was sensei*, not Fujiiwa herself, who made the request.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生がそう言ったんです。
contrast_examples.en: It was sensei who said that.

prompt.context_jp: 客席の悦子___、貝塚の視線を気にすることも忘れてその姿を追った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 客席の悦子___、…その姿を追った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 悦子, our protagonist being described here.

feedback.correct_en: Etsuko is the established main character; the sentence describes what she is doing from her seat. は carries this topic-continuation role naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single her out as a newly-identified subject, which conflicts with her being the ongoing protagonist whose actions we've been following.

contrast_examples.en: Etsuko (our known hero) stared at him.
It was Etsuko who stared at him. (identifies who)

prompt.context_jp: お前でも 人の役に立つこと___あるとは驚いた
prompt.prompt_jp: 人の役に立つこと___あるとは驚いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Kaizuka marvels that Etsuko can actually be useful. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The pattern 「〜ことがある」 (there are times when...) requires が — こと is the existing subject of ある. It's a fixed existential frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: ことは would read as contrastive ('as for such times...') and the sentence wouldn't complete the 'there exists such a thing' meaning Kaizuka intends.

contrast_examples.en: There are times when it's useful.

prompt.context_jp: もしかしてなんだけど 私にファンレター___書いてくれたことある？
prompt.prompt_jp: 私にファンレター___書いてくれたことある？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for ファンレター.

feedback.correct_en: 書く takes a direct object, so ファンレター — the thing being written — is marked with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make ファンレター a subject, which doesn't fit 書く. は could be contrastive but would need a specific contrastive context that isn't here.

prompt.context_jp: ちょっと訳あって ちょこっと 出ることになったんで もし よかったら 見___来てください
prompt.prompt_jp: よかったら 見___来てください。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in 見___来る.

feedback.correct_en: The pattern 「〜Vます-stem + に + 来る/行く」 expresses purpose of motion ('come to do X'). 見に来る = 'come to watch.'
feedback.incorrect_en: を would need a noun, not a verb stem functioning adverbially. で marks means/location, not purpose.

prompt.context_jp: 憧れの亀井さやかのもとで働く自分の姿だけを胸に、彼女はきょうも___に化粧を整えてきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女はきょうも___に化粧を整えてきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits Etsuko's careful, meticulous makeup routine.

feedback.correct_en: 念入り means 'thorough, with great care.' Etsuko is a fashion obsessive going to a dream interview — she applies makeup with painstaking care.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大雑把 ('rough, careless') contradicts her character. 簡単 ('simple/easy') is grammatically off with に before 化粧を整える here and misses her dedication.

prompt.context_jp: 悦子は思わず身を隠しかけ、それでも我慢しきれずに声を___しまった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 我慢しきれずに声を___しまった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 声を to mean 'raise one's voice.'

feedback.correct_en: 声を張り上げる is the set collocation for 'raise one's voice / shout out.' It captures that she blurted out despite trying to hide.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持ち上げる and 引き上げる are physical 'lift up' verbs that don't form idiomatic expressions with 声.

prompt.context_jp: 校閲部の河野悦子と申します⇒ どうぞ 以後___を
prompt.prompt_jp: 校閲部の河野悦子と申します。どうぞ 以後___を。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the set phrase for a polite self-introduction to a superior.

feedback.correct_en: 「以後お見知りおきを」 is a formal set phrase meaning 'please remember me / keep me in mind from now on,' used when introducing oneself to someone important.
feedback.incorrect_en: お世話 would need a different frame (お世話になります). お疲れさま is a greeting for finishing work, not an introduction.

contrast_examples.en: Please remember me from now on. (introduction)
I'll be in your care. (relationship opener)

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚と幸人のやり取りに調子よく付き合ううち、彼女は口を___いたのだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女は口を___いたのだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'she had let something slip.'

feedback.correct_en: 口を滑らす is the idiom for 'let something slip / blurt out by accident.' It fits Etsuko letting out the Linear Motor Cow comment without realizing who she was speaking to.
feedback.incorrect_en: 口を開ける is literal 'open one's mouth.' 口を閉じる is literal 'close one's mouth' — neither captures the 'accidental slip' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: うっかり口を滑らせる。

prompt.context_jp: よく言うよ ___で “ぜえいぜえ”って呼んでるくせに
prompt.prompt_jp: ___で “ぜえいぜえ”って呼んでるくせに。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'behind someone's back.'

feedback.correct_en: 陰で means 'behind someone's back / in secret.' Kaizuka is calling out Etsuko for secretly mocking the author.
feedback.incorrect_en: 前で ('in front of') is the opposite. 裏口 ('back entrance') is a physical place, not a figurative expression.

prompt.context_jp: 余計なツッコミとかいらないから 誤字脱字のチェックと 事実確認に___して
prompt.prompt_jp: 誤字脱字のチェックと 事実確認に___して。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'focus/devote yourself to.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜に専念する means 'devote oneself exclusively to ~.' Yoneoka tells Etsuko to concentrate only on typo-checking and fact-checking.
feedback.incorrect_en: 専攻 means 'major (in school).' 専用 means 'exclusive use (of equipment).' Neither pairs with 〜に to describe focusing one's effort.

prompt.context_jp: 作者の私ですら忘れてた設定の矛盾を ___してくれるなんて まさに校閲のプロね
prompt.prompt_jp: 設定の矛盾を ___してくれるなんて。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'point out (a problem).'

feedback.correct_en: 指摘する means 'point out (an issue, flaw, inconsistency).' It's the standard word for what a proofreader does when flagging problems in a text.
feedback.incorrect_en: 指示 means 'give instructions.' 指名 means 'designate/nominate (a person).' Neither matches 'noticing an inconsistency and calling attention to it.'

prompt.context_jp: あの指摘は 先生の作品を___好きな人じゃないと できなかった指摘です
prompt.prompt_jp: 先生の作品を___好きな人じゃないとできなかった指摘です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adverb meaning 'from the bottom of one's heart / truly.'

feedback.correct_en: 心底(しんそこ) is an adverb meaning 'from the bottom of one's heart.' Etsuko emphasizes that only a truly devoted fan could have caught the inconsistency.
feedback.incorrect_en: 本音 is a noun meaning 'true feelings (vs. tatemae).' 心境 is 'state of mind.' Neither functions as an adverb modifying 好き.

prompt.context_jp: Opening line of the chapter, introducing the interview scene.
prompt.prompt_en: Which opening sounds more natural as a narrative introduction of a brand-new character?

choices.text: 東京・景凡社の面接室に、七度目の挑戦者が立っていた。
東京・景凡社の面接室に、七度目の挑戦者は立っていた。

feedback.correct_en: In opening narration, a brand-new character is introduced with が. The reader has no prior topic to pick up, so が frames them as a fresh presence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は presupposes the reader already knows the challenger — awkward as a first line, since no one has been mentioned yet.

contrast_examples.jp: 昔々、おじいさんがいました。
contrast_examples.en: Long ago, there was an old man. (introducing)

contrast_examples.jp: おじいさんは山へ行きました。
contrast_examples.en: The old man went to the mountain. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: Fujiiwa explains why proofreaders shouldn't handle authors they love.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for the sentiment 'precisely because you like it, you shouldn't handle it'?

choices.text: 好きだからこそ 担当すべきではないんです。
好きだから 担当すべきではないんです。

feedback.correct_en: 〜だからこそ emphasizes 'it's precisely because of this' — exactly Fujiiwa's logic. 好きだからこそ captures that the love itself is the very reason to step away.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜だから is correct grammar but flat. It loses the emphatic 'precisely because' force that makes Fujiiwa's stance distinctive.

contrast_examples.jp: 君だからこそ頼むんだ。
contrast_examples.en: I'm asking you precisely because it's you.

prompt.context_jp: Yukito asks Etsuko to exchange contact info.
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds more natural as an enthusiastic 'yes, gladly!'?

feedback.correct_en: 喜んで is the fixed adverbial form from 喜ぶ ('to be glad'), widely used as a standalone enthusiastic 'Gladly! / With pleasure!'
feedback.incorrect_en: 嬉しんで is not a real form. 嬉しい is an i-adjective and does not conjugate this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 喜んでお引き受けします。

prompt.context_jp: Sensei sighs, resigned, after Etsuko says it wasn't her writing those fan letters.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'there's no way such a coincidence would happen'?

choices.text: そんな偶然 あるわけないわよね。
そんな偶然 ないわけあるわよね。

feedback.correct_en: 〜わけがない is the set pattern for strong denial: 'there's no way that ~.' あるわけない = 'there's no way it exists.'
feedback.incorrect_en: ないわけある is a jumbled inversion that doesn't form a standard expression.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなことあるわけない。
contrast_examples.en: There's no way that could happen.

prompt.context_jp: Fujiiwa defends her principle of following rules even against her own desires.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'to push through one's desires to the point of breaking rules'?

choices.text: ルールを破ってまで 自分の欲望を押し通すのは 私の主義に反します。
ルールを破るほどに 自分の欲望を押し通すのは 私の主義に反します。

feedback.correct_en: 〜てまで expresses 'going so far as to do ~,' marking an extreme measure. It perfectly captures Fujiiwa's framing: 'to the extent of breaking rules.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ほどに means 'to the degree that,' which describes extent in a comparative way and doesn't carry the 'going so far as' sacrifice nuance that 〜てまで does.

contrast_examples.jp: 嘘をついてまで勝ちたくない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't want to win to the extent of lying.
Frustrated to the point of crying.
